G1600.def:
ἐκ-πετάννυμι 
[in LXX chiefly for פָּרַשׂ, as Ésaïe 65:2 (hithp.) ;] 
to spread out (as a sail), stretch forth: Romains 10:21(LXX).†

G1601.def:
ἐκ-πίπτω 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 40:8 28:1, 4 (הֶבֶל), Job 14:2 (מָלַל, see RV. mg), Job 15:30 (סוּר), Job 15:33 (שָׁלַךְ hi.), etc. ;] 
to fall out of, fall from, fall off: before ἐκ τ. χειρῶν, Actes 12:7; absol., Actes 27:32; of the withering of flowers (as LXX, ll with), Jacques 1:11, 1 Pierre 1:24" (LXX) ; of navigators falling off from a straight course, Actes 27:17, 26 27:29 Metaphorical, with genitive of thing(s): Galates 5:4, 2 Pierre 3:17; absol., fall from its place, fail, perish: Romains 9:6.†

G1602.def:
ἐκ-πλέω, -ῶ 
to sail away: Actes 20:6; before εἰς, Actes 15:39 18:18.†

G1603.def:
ἐκ-πληρόω 
[in LXX: 2Ma.8:10, 3Ma.1:2 3Mac 1:22 * ;] 
__1. to fill full, make up a number. 
__2. to fulfil (MM, Exp., xii; Cremer, 839), Actes 13:32.†

G1604.def:
ἐκ-πλήρωσις, -εως, ἡ) 
[in LXX: 2Ma.6:14 * ;] 
a completion, fulfilment: Actes 21:26.†

G1605.def:
ἐκ-πλήσσω
(Attic -ττω, Actes 13:12), [in LXX: (pass.) Ecclésiaste 7:16, (שָׁמֵם hithp.), Wis.13:4, 2Ma.7:12, 4Ma.8:4 4Mac 17:16 * ;] 
__1. prop., to strike out, drive away. 
__2. to strike with panic or shock, to amaze, astonish: pass., Matthieu 13:54 19:25, Marc 6:2 7:37 10:26, Luc 2:48; before ἐπί, with dative of thing(s), Matthieu 7:28 22:33, Marc 1:22 11:18, Luc 4:32 9:43, Actes 13:12.†
SYN.: " πτωεῖν G?, to terrify, agitate with fear; 
τρεμεῖν, to tremble, predominantly physical; 
φοβεῖν, to fear, "the general term," Thayer; 
cf. also φρίσσω, to shudder, and see: δειλία 
δειλία, -ας, ἡ 
(δειλός), [in LXX for אֵימָה, מְחִתָּה, etc. ;] 
cowardice, timidity (never in good sense): 2 Timothée 1:7.†
SYN.: φόβος, fear, in general, good or bad; εὐλάβεια (which see), apprehension generally, but chiefly pious fear, "that careful and watchful reverence which pays regard to every circumstance in that with which it has to deal" (cf. Tr., Syn., § x).†

G1606.def:
ἐκ-πνέω, -ῶ, 
to breathe out; sc. βίον, ψυχήν (expressed in cl., Æsch., al.; cf. LS, see word), to breathe one's last, expire: Marc 15:37, 39 Luc 23:46. For force of aorist, see Swete, Marc 15:37.†

G1607.def:
ἐκ-πορεύω 
[in LXX chiefly for יָצָא ;] 
to make to go out; pass. and mid., to go forth: Luc 3:7, Actes 25:4; of demons leaving one possessed, Matthieu 17:21 (WH om.), Actes 19:12; of excrement, Mk 719; before ἀπό, Matthieu 20:29, Marc 10:46; ἐκ, Marc 13:1 (of the dead rising, Jean 5:29); ἐκεῖθεν, Marc 6:11; ἔξω, Marc 11:19; είς, Marc 10:17, Jean 5:29; ἐπί, with accusative of person(s), Apocalypse 16:14; πρός, with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 3:5, Marc 1:5; εἰσπορ- (which see) καὶ ἐ., Actes 9:28; metaphorically, to come forth, proceed: of feelings, etc., Marc 7:23; before ἐκ, Matthieu 15:11, 18 Marc 7:15, 20-21, Luc 4:22, Éphésiens 4:29; ῥῆμα, before διά, Matthieu 4:4 (LXX); of lightning and flame, Apocalypse 4:5 9:17-18 11:5; a river, Apocalypse 22:1; a sword, Apocalypse 1:16 19:15; a rumour, before εἰς, Luc 4:37; of the Holy Spirit, before παρά, Jean 15:26.†

G1608.def:
ἐκ-πορνεύω 
[in LXX chiefly for זָנָה, frequently of spiritual unfaithfulness ;] 
strengthened form of πoρνεύω, implying excessive indulgence; mid, to give oneself up to fornication: Ju 7.†

G1609.def:
ἐκ-πτύω 
__1. to spit out. 
__2. to spit at in disgust, to abominate, loathe (= cl. ἀποπτ-, καταπτ-): Galates 4:14.†

G1610.def:
ἐκ-ριζόω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Juges 5:14 (שֶׁרֶשׁ), Jérémie 1:10 (נָתַשׁ), Sophonie 2:4 (גָּרַשׁ A, עָקַר BS), Daniel 7:8 (עָקַר), Dan LXX 4:11, 23, Wis.4:4, Sir.3:9 49:7, 1Ma.5:51, 2Ma.12:7 * ;] 
to root out, pluck up by the roots: with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 13:29 15:13 Luc 17:6, Ju 12.†

G1612.def:
ἐκ-στρέφω 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 32:20, Amos 6:13 Eze.16:34 A (הָפַךְ), Za 11:16 (פָּרַק pi.), Eze.13:20 (צוּד pi.)* ;] 
__1. to turn out of (Hom.). 
__2. to turn inside out; metaphorically, to change entirely, pervert (Aristoph.): Tite 3:11.†

G1613.def:
ἐκ-ταράσσω 
[in LXX: Psaumes 18:4 (עֵת pi.), Psaumes 88:16 (צוּם), צוּם), Wis.17:3-4 18:17 * ;] 
to throw into great trouble, agitate: Actes 16:20.†

G1614.def:
ἐκ-τείνω 
[in LXX for שָׁלַח, נָטָה, etc. ;] 
to stretch out or forth: τ. χεῖρα (as often in LXX), Matthieu 8:3 12:13 14:31 26:51, Marc 1:41 3:5, Luc 5:13 6:10 Jean 21:18, Actes 26:1; before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s), towards, Matthieu 12:49; against, Luc 22:53; εἰς ἴασιν, Actes 4:30; of anchors, to cast, Actes 27:30.†

G1615.def:
ἐκ-τελέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 32:45 (כָּלָה), 2 Chroniques 4:5, (Da TH Daniel 3:40), 2Ma.15:9 * ;] 
to bring to an end, finish, complete: Luc 14:29-30.†

G1616.def:
ἐκ-τένεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἐκτενής), [in LXX: Jdth.4:9, 2Ma.14:38, 3Ma.6:41 * ;] 
zeal, intentness, earnestness (cf. Deiss., BS, 262): Actes 26:7.†

G1617.def:
deeply, earnestly 
intensely, fervently, earnestly, deeply Lk. 22:44; Acts 12:5; 1Pet. 1:22*

G1618.def:
ἐκτενής, -ές
(ἐκτείνω), [in LXX: 3Ma.3:10 3Mac 5:29 * ;] 
stretched, strained. Metaphorical, earnest, zealous: 1 Pierre 4:8 .†

G1619.def:
ἐκτενῶς 
adv., [in LXX: Jonas 3:8 (חׇזְקָה), Joël 1:14, Jdth.4:12, 3Ma.5:9 * ;] 
fervently, earnestly: Actes 12:5, 1 Pierre 1:22; compar., Luc 22:44 (WH br., R, mg., omits).†

G1620.def:
ἐκ-τίθημι 
[in LXX for נָתַן ni., etc. ;] 
to set out, expose: Actes 7:21, Metaphorical, to set forth, expound: Actes 11:4 28:23; with accusative of thing(s), Actes 18:26.†

G1621.def:
ἐκ-τινάσσω 
[in LXX for נָעַר ni., pi., etc. ;] 
to shake off: κονιορτόν, Matthieu 10:14; χοῦν, Marc 6:11. Mid.: κονιορτόν, Actes 13:51; ἱμάτια, Actes 18:6 (cf. MM, Exp., iii).†

G1622.def:
1. outside , opposite to ἐντός: 
2. as preposition with genitive outside, out of, far from , with genitive, (Homer): outside of, free from , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; ἐκτὸς ἐλπίδος beyond hope, Lat. praeter spem, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. of Time, beyond , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. except , ἐκτὸς ὀλίγων (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. absolute, τὰ ἐκτός external things , (Euripides) 
6. with Verbs of motion, ῥίπτειν ἐκτός to throw out , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. (ML)

G1624.def:
ἐκ-τρέπω 
[in LXX for הָפַךְ, Amos 5:8 * ;] 
to turn out of the course, turn aside, with accusative Pass., with middle sense, intrans., to turn aside: Hébreux 12:13 (R, txt., for be put out of joint, R, mg., see Thayer, see word Westc., in l); figuratively, before εἰς, 1 Timothée 1:6; ἐπί, 2 Timothée 4:4; ὀπίσω, 1 Timothée 5:15; with accusative, to shun, avoid: 1 Timothée 6:20.†

G1625.def:
ἐκ-τρέφω 
[in LXX for גָּדַל, etc. ;] 
__1. prop., of children, to nurture, bring up: Éphésiens 6:4. 
__2. to nourish: Éphésiens 5:29.†

G1626.def:
ἔκ-τρωμα, -τος, τό
(ἐκτιτρώσκω, to miscarry), [in LXX: Job 3:16, Ecclésiaste 6:3 (; also in Aq., Psaumes 58:9, Nombres 12:12 (נָפַל) * ;] 
an abortion, an untimely birth (see Field, Notes, 179): 1 Corinthiens 15:8.†

G1628.def:
ἐκ-φεύγω 
[in LXX for נוּס, etc. ;] 
to flee away, escape: absol., Actes 16:27, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:3, Hébreux 2:3; before ἐκ, Actes 19:10; with accusative of person(s), Hébreux 12:25; with accusative of thing(s), Luc 21:36, Romains 2:3; τ. χεῖρας αὐτοῦ, 2 Corinthiens 11:33.†

G1629.def:
ἐκ-φοβέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX chiefly for חָרֵד hi. ;] 
to frighten away, terrify: with accusative of person(s), 2 Corinthiens 10:9.†

G1630.def:
ἔκφοβος, -ον 
[in LXX: ἔ. εἶναι for יָגֹר, Deutéronome 9:19; also 1Ma.13:2 * ;] 
affrighted, terrified: Marc 9:16, Hébreux 12:21.†

G1631.def:
ἐκ-φύω 
[in OT (Sm.) Psaumes 104:14; (Al.) Ésaïe 61:11 * ;] 
to cause to grow out, put forth (leaves): Matthieu 24:32, Marc 13:28.†

G1632.def:
ἐκ-χέω also Hellenistic, ἐκχύνω (in Th.: 4Ki.14:14 *), and ἐκχύννω (which see) 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁפַךְ ;] 
to pour out: φιάλην, Apocalypse 16:1-4, 8 16:10, 12 16:17; κέρματα, Jean 2:15; αἷμα, Matthieu 23:35 (cf. MM, Exp., xii), Luc 11:50, Actes 22:20, Romains 3:15" (LXX) Apocalypse 16:6. Pass., αἷμα, Matthieu 26:28, Marc 14:24, Actes 22:20; οἶνος, Matthieu 9:17, Luc 5:37; σπλάγχνα, Actes 1:18. Metaphorical, τ. πνεῦμα, Actes 2:17-18 (LXX), Actes 2:33 10:45, Tite 3:6; ἀγάπη, Romains 5:5 (cf. Sir.36:8, ὀργήν); pass., of persons (like Lat. effundor), to give oneself up to (RV, ran riotously in): Ju 11.†

G1633.def:
εκ-χύννω 
Hellenistic form of ἐκχέω, which see (E1., § 17): Matthieu 23:35 26:28, Marc 14:24, Luc 5:37 11:50 22:20, Actes 1:18 10:45 22:20, Romains 5:5, Ju 11.†
ἐκ-χωρέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Nombres 16:45 (רוּם ni.), Juges 7:3 (צָפַר), Amos 7:12 (בָּרַח), 1Es.4:44 Esther 4:57, 1Ma.9:62 * ;] 
to depart, withdraw: Luc 21:21.†

G1634.def:
ἐκ-ψύχω 
[in LXX: Juges 4:21 A (עוּף), Eze.21:7 (כָּהָה pi.)* ;] 
to expire, breathe one's last: Actes 5:5, 10 12:23 (cf. ἐκπνέω; Cremer, 906).†

G1635.def:
ἑκών, -οῦσα, -όν 
[in LXX: Exode 21:13, Job 36:19 * ;] 
willing, of one's own free will: Romains 8:20, 1 Corinthiens 9:17 (Cremer, 246).†

G1636.def:
ἐλαία
(Attic, ἐλάα), -ας, ἡ [in LXX for זַיִת ;] 
__1. an olive tree: Romains 11:17, 24, Apocalypse 11:4; τ. ὄρος τῶν ἐ. (זַיִת הַר, Zacharie 14:4), the Mount of Olives: Matthieu 21:1 24:3 26:30, Marc 11:1 13:3 14:26, Luc 19:37 22:39; τὸ καλούμενον ἐ. (T, ἐλαιών, which see), Luc 19:29 21:37. 
__2. an olive (Aristoph.): Jacques 3:12.†

G1637.def:
ἔλαιον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for שֶׁמֶן ;] 
olive-oil: Luc 16:6, Apocalypse 6:6 18:13; for lamps, Matthieu 25:3-4, 8; for healing, Marc 6:13, Luc 10:34, Jean 5:14; for anointing at feasts, Luc 7:46, Hébreux 1:9" (LXX) .†
SYN.: μύρον, ointment, see Tr., Syn., 135

G1638.def:
ἐλαιών, -ῶνος, ὁ
(ἐλαία), [in LXX for זַיִת ;] 
olive-grove, olive-garden (so in FlJ and in π.; Deiss., BS, 209 ff.; MM, Exp., iii; M, Pr., 49, 69, 235): Luc 19:29 21:37 (WH, -ῶν; see their App., 158; Field, Notes, 73; El., § 10, 5; 33, 1; Thayer, see word), Actes 1:12 (where EL, ll with, proposes the conjectural emendation ἐλαιῶν for -ῶνος).†

G1639.def:
Ἐλαμείτης (Rec. -αμίτης), -ου, ὁ 
(Heb. אֵילָם) [in LXX (cl.) Ἐλυμαίος, Ἔλαμος: Jdth.1:6; Ἀιλαμείτης (vv.ll. Ἐλ-, -αμίτης; Bl., § 3, 7): Ésaïe 11:11 21:2 22:6) ;] 
an Elamite: Actes 2:9.†

G1640.def:
ἐλάσσων (-ττων, Heb_7:7, WH, 1Ti_5:9), -ον
(formed, with superl. ἐλάχιστος, from the epic ἐλαχύς, little, and serving as compar. of μικρός), [in LXX for מָעַט, etc. ;] 
less, in age, rank or quality: Jean 2:19, Romains 9:12" (LXX), Hébreux 7:7; neut., -ον, adverbially: 1 Timothée 5:9.†

G1641.def:
ἐλαττονέω, -ῶ
(ἔλαττον), [in LXX (with -όω) chiefly for חָסֵר ;] 
to be less (RV, had no lack): 2 Corinthiens 8:15 (LXX) (a rare word; cf. MM, Exp., xii).†

G1642.def:
ἐλαττόω, -ῶ
(ἐλάιττων), [in LXX (where also -σσῶ) chiefly for חָסֵר, and very frequently in Sir ;] 
to make less: Hébreux 2:7 (LXX); pass., Jean 3:30, Hébreux 2:9.†

G1643.def:
ἐλαύνω 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 41:7 (הָלַם) Ésaïe 33:21 (שַׁיִט), etc. ;] 
to drive: of the wind, Jacques 3:4, 2 Pierre 2:17; of sailors rowing or sailing a boat, Marc 6:48, Jean 6:19; of demons, Luc 8:29 (cf. ἀπ-, συν-ελαύνω).†

G1645.def:
ἐλαφρός, -ά, -όν 
[in LXX chiefly for קַל, קָלָל ;] 
light in weight easy to bear: Matthieu 11:30; θλίψρις (EV, our light affliction), 2 Corinthiens 4:17.†

G1646.def:
ἐλάχιστος, -η, -ον
(see: ἐλάσσων), 
smallest, least: as proper superlat., 1 Corinthiens 15:9; elsewhere, as usually in late Gk., intensive (B1., § 11, 3); Matthieu 2:6 (LXX) Matthieu 25:40, 45 Luc 12:26 16:10 19:17, 1 Corinthiens 4:3 6:2, Jacques 3:4; ἐ. ἐν τ. βασιλείᾳ τ. οὐρανῶν, Matthieu 5:19 (see Dalman, Words, 113). Compar., ἐλαχιστότερος (for corresp. superl., see LS; see also Bl., § 44, 3); less than the least: Éphésiens 3:8.†

G1648.def:
Ἐλεάζαρ(Heb. אֶלְעָזָר), ὁ, indecl., 
Eleazar: Matthieu 1:15.†

G1649.def:
ἐλεγξις, -εως, ἡ
(ἐλέγχω), [in LXX: Job 21:4 23:2 (שִׂיחַ) * ;] 
re­buke: 2 Pierre 2:16.†

G1650.def:
ἔλεγχος, -ου, ὁ 
(ἐλέγχω) [in LXX: frequently in Pr, Jb (יָכַח) יָכַח) Wis.5:1-23, Sir.3:1-31, etc. ;] 
a proof, test: Hébreux 11:1.†

G1651.def:
ἐλέγχω 
[in LXX chiefly for יָכַח hi. ;] 
__1. in Hom., to treat with contempt. 
__2. to convict: with accusative, Matthieu 18:15 (RV, show him his fault), Tite 1:9; before περί, Jean 8:46 16:8, Ju 15; pass., Jacques 2:9. 
__3. to reprove, re­buke: 1 Timothée 5:20, 2 Timothée 4:2, Tite 1:13 2:15, Apocalypse 3:19; pass., before περί, Luc 3:19; ὑπό, Hébreux 12:5 (LXX). 
__4. to expose: Éphésiens 5:11; pass., Jean 3:20, 1 Corinthiens 14:24 (RV reprove, mg. convict), Éphésiens 5:13 (RV, as 1 Co, l.with, of. AR on Éphésiens 5:11; MM, Exp., xii; cf. ἐξ-, δια-κατ-ελέγχομαι).†
SYN.: ἐπιτιμῶ, expressing simply rebuke, which may be un­deserved (Matthieu 16:22) or ineffectual (Luc 23:40), while ἐλ. implies rebuke which brings conviction (see Tr., Syn., § iv)

G1652.def:
ἐλεεινός, -ή, -όν
(ἔλεος in Re, l.with, WH have the Attic poëtic form, ἐλεινός), 
pitiable, miserable: Apocalypse 3:17; comparat., 1 Corinthiens 15:19.†

G1653.def:
ἐλεέω
(in Romains 9:16, Ju 22, -άω, which see), -ῶ (ἔλεος), [in LXX (Hex, Pss, Pr) chiefly for חָנַן, also frequently in Proph. for רָחַם, etc. ;] 
to have pity or mercy on, to show mercy: absol., Romains 9:16 12:8; with accusative, Matthieu 9:27 15:22 17:15 18:33 20:30-31, Marc 5:19 10:47-48, Luc 16:24 17:13 18:38-39 Romains 9:15, 18 11:32, Philippiens 2:27, Ju 22. Pass., to have pity or mercy shown one (EV, obtain mercy): Matthieu 5:7, Romains 11:30-31, 1 Corinthiens 7:25, 2 Corinthiens 4:1, 1 Timothée 1:13 1:16, 1 Pierre 2:10.†

G1654.def:
ἐλεημοσύνη, -ης, ἡ
(ἐλεέω), [in LXX chiefly for חֶסֶד, צְדָקָה ;] 
__1. mercy, pity. 
__2. almsgiving, alms (like the German Almosen, a corruption of the Greek word ἐ): Matthieu 6:4; ποιεῖν ἐ., Matthieu 6:2-3, Actes 9:36 10:2 24:17; ἐ. διδόναι, Luc 11:41 (cf. Matthieu 23:36; Dalman, Words, 62 f.) 12:33; αἰτεῖν, Actes 3:2; λαβεῖν, Actes 3:3; πρὸς (in order to ask) ἐ., Actes 3:10; pl., Actes 10:4, 31 (Cremer, 711).†

G1655.def:
ἐλεήμων, -ον 
[in LXX chiefly for חַנּוּן ;] 
merciful: Matthieu 5:7, Hébreux 2:17.†

G1656.def:
ἔλεος, -ους, τό
(cl. -ου, ὁ, and so Rec., Matthieu 9:13 12:7 23:23, Tite 3:5, Hébreux 4:16; on the Hellenistic form τό ἔ., see WH, App., 158; M, Pr., 60; Mayser, 277; Kühner, i, 515), [in LXX chiefly for חֶסֶד ;] 
mercy, pity, compassion; 
__1. of men: Matthieu 9:13 (LXX) Matthieu 12:7 23:23; ποιεῖν ἔ. (and id. before μετά, with genitive; cf. Heb. עִם חֶסֶד עָשָׂה, Genèse 21:23, al.), Luc 10:37, Jacques 2:13 3:17. 
__2. Of God: Luc 1:50, 54 1:58, Romains 15:9, Éphésiens 2:4, 2 Timothée 1:16 1:18, Tite 3:5, Hébreux 4:16, 1 Pierre 1:3; esp. in benedictions, Galates 6:16, 1 Timothée 1:2, 2 Timothée 1:2, 2Jn.3, Ju 2; σκευὴ ἐλέους, Romains 9:23; σπλάγχνα ἐλέους, Luc 1:78; ποιεῖν ἔ. (see supr.), Luc 1:72; τ. ὑμετέρῳ ἐλέει, Romains 11:31. 
__3. Of Christ: Ju 21.†
SYN.: οἰκτιρμός (see: ἐλεέω)

G1657.def:
ἐλευθερία, -ας, ἡ 
[in LXX: Lévitique 19:20 (חֻפְשָׁה), 1Es.4:49 Esther 4:53, Sir.7:21, Sir.33:25, 1Ma.14:27, 3Ma.3:28 * ;] 
liberty: with reference to the religious life, 1 Corinthiens 10:29, 2 Corinthiens 3:17, Galates 2:4 5:1, 1 Pierre 2:16, 2 Pierre 2:19; ὁ νόμος τῆς ἐ., Jacques 1:25 2:12; ἡ ἐ. τῆς δόξης, Romains 8:21; ἐπ᾽ ἐ., Galates 5:13 (on which formula, cf. Deiss., LAE, 327 ff.; Cremer, 251).†

G1659.def:
ἐλευθερόω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Proverbes 25:10. 2Ma.1:27 2Mac 2:22 * ;] 
to make free from sin, Jean 8:32, 36; before ἀπό, Romains 6:18, 22 8:2, 21; τ. ἐλευθερία (dative commodi), Galates 5:1 (on the "punctiliar" force of this verb, see M, Pr. 149; cf. also Cremer, 251).†

G1660.def: a coming:—;the Advent of our LORD, (New Testament) (ML)

G1661.def:
ἐλεφάντινος, -η, -ον
(ἐλέφας, ivory), [in LXX for שֵׁן ;] 
of ivory: Apocalypse 18:12.†

G1662G.def:
Ἐλιακείμ(Heb. אֶלְיָקִים), 
Eliakim, an ancestor of Jesus: Matthieu 1:13, Luc 3:30.†

G1662H.def:
Ἐλιακείμ(Heb. אֶלְיָקִים), 
Eliakim, an ancestor of Jesus: Matthieu 1:13, Luc 3:30.†

G1663.def:
Ἐλιέζερ(Heb. אֱלִיעֶזֶר), ὁ, indecl., 
Eliezer, an ancestor of Jesus: Luc 3:29.†

G1664.def:
Ἐλιούδ, ὁ 
indecl., 
Eliud, an ancestor of Jesus: Matthieu 1:14-15.†

G1665.def:
Ἐλεισάβετ (T, Rec. Ἐλισ-; see WH, App., 155), ἡ indecl. (Heb. אֱלִישֶׁבַע) 
Elizabeth: Luc 1:5 ff.†

G1666.def:
Ἐλισαῖος (Rec. Ἐλισσαῖος; Τ, Ἑλισ-), -ου, ὁ (Heb. אֱלִישָׁע), 
Elisha, the prophet: Luc 4:27.†

G1667.def:
ἑλίσσω 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 34:4 (גָּלַל ni.), Psaumes 102:26 (חָלַף hi.), etc. ;] 
to roll, roll up: Hébreux 1:12 (LXX), Apocalypse 6:14.†

G1668.def:
ἑλκος, -εος (-ους), τό
[in LXX: Exode 9:9-11, Lévitique 13:18-27, 4Ki.20:7, Job 2:7 (שְׁחִין) ;] 
__1. a wound (Hom.). 
__2. a sore, an ulcer (Thuc., al.): Luc 16:21, Apocalypse 16:2, 11.†

G1669.def:
ἑλκόω, -ῶ 
__1. to wound. 
__2. to ulcerate; pass., to suffer from sores: pf. ptcp., εἱλκωμίνος (Rec. ἡλκ-), EV, full of sores, Luc 16:20.†

G1670.def:
ἕλκω 
(Hellenistic form ἑλκύω in Jean 11:1-57. with, Actes 16:19), [in LXX for מָשַׁךְ, etc. ;] 
to draw: with accusative of thing(s), Jean 18:10 21:6; with accusative of person(s), before ἔξω, Actes 21:30; εἰς, Actes 16:19, Jacques 2:6. Metaphorical, to draw, lead, impel: Jean 6:44 12:32. (For discussion of ἕ. in Oxyrh. Log., see Deiss., LAE, 437 ff.)†

G1671.def:
Ἑλλάς, -άδος, ἡ 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 66:19, Eze.27:13 (יָוָן), 1Ma.1:1 1Mac 8:9 * ;] 
with varying usage as to geographical limits; in NT = 'Αχαία (cf. Actes 18:12), 
Greece: Actes 20:2.†

G1672.def:
Ἕλλην, -ηνος, ὁ 
[in LXX: Joël 3:6, Zacharie 9:13 (יָוָן), etc.; 1Ma.1:19, al. * ;] 
a Greek; opposite to βάρβαρος, Romains 1:14; usually in ΝΤ of Greek Gentiles, opposite to Ἰουδαῖοι: Jean 7:35, Actes 11:29 14:1 16:1, 3 18:4 19:19, 17 20:21 21:28 Romains 1:16 2:9-10 3:9 10:12, 1 Corinthiens 1:22 1:24 10:32 12:13, Galates 2:3 3:28, Colossiens 3:11; of proselytes, Jean 12:29, Actes 17:4.†

G1673.def:
Ἑλληνικκός, -ή, -όν 
[in LXX: Jérémie 46:6 50:16 (יָנָה: aliter in Heb.), 2Ma.4:10 2Mac 4:15 2Mac 6:9 2Mac 11:24 2Mac 13:2, 4Ma.8:8 * ;] 
Greek: τ. Ἑλληνικῇ (sc. γλωσσῇ), Apocalypse 9:11.†

G1674.def:
Ἑλληνίς
[in LXX: 2Ma.6:8 A * ;] 
a Greek (i.e. Gentile) woman: Marc 7:26, Actes 17:12.†

G1675.def:
Ἑλληνιστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(Ἑλληνίζω, to Hellenize, affect Greek cus­toms), 
a Hellenist (RV, Grecian Jew): Actes 6:1 9:29 11:20.†

G1676.def:
Ἑλληνιστί 
adv., 
in Greek: Jean 19:20; Ἑ. (sc. λαλεῖν) γινώσκεις, Actes 21:37 (cf. Field, Notes, 135).†

G1677.def:
ἐλλογάω, -ῶ
(a κοινή word, elsewhere usually -έω; cf. Bl., § 22, 2), 
to charge to one's account, impute: Phm 18 (on parallels, cf. Deiss., LAE, 79 f., 335 f.; Milligan, NTD, 73; MM, Exp., xii); of sin, Romains 5:13 (Cremer, 400).†

G1678.def:
Ἐλμαδάμ (L, Ἑλ-; Rec. -μωδάμ), ό, indecl., 
Elmadam, an ancestor of Jesus: Luc 3:28.

G1679.def:
ἐλπίζω 
[in LXX chiefly for בָּטַח, also for חָסָה, יָחַל pi., hi., etc. ;] 
to look for, expect, hope (for): with accusative of thing(s), Romains 8:24-25, 1 Corinthiens 13:7, Hébreux 11:1; with dative of thing(s) (τ. τύχῃ, Thuc., iii, 97, 2), Matthieu 12:21; before καθώς, 2 Corinthiens 8:5; with inf., Luc 6:34 23:8, Actes 26:7, Romains 15:24, 1 Corinthiens 16:7, 2 Corinthiens 5:11, Philippiens 2:19, 23, 1 Timothée 3:14, II Jn 12, 3Jn.14; before ὅτι, with pres., Luc 24:21; with fut., Actes 24:26, 2 Corinthiens 1:13 13:6, Phm 22. As in LXX (WM, § xxxiii, d; and esp. in the pf., Ellic. on 1 Timothée 4:10; Bl., § 59, 2), with prep.; εἰς, Jean 5:45 (see Ellis., l.with), 1 Pierre 3:5; before ὅτι, 2 Corinthiens 1:10; ἐπί, with dative, Romains 15:12 (LXX 1 Timothée 4:10 6:17; ἐν, 1 Corinthiens 15:19; with accusative, 1 Pierre 1:13 (aor. imper. see Bl., § 58, 2); τ. θεόν, 1 Timothée 5:5 (of. ἀπ-, προ-ελπίζω, see Cremer, 255).†

G1680.def:
ἐλπίς 
(ἑλ-, Romains 8:20, WH, see Bl., § 4, 3; M, Pr., 44), -ίδος, ἡ [in LXX for בָּטַח and its derivatives, תִּקְוָה (frequently in Jb), etc. ;] 
expectation (in cl., rarely of evil, mostly of good, and so always in NT), hope; 
__1. of hope in general: 2 Corinthiens 1:6; with genitive obj., Actes 16:19; art. inf., Actes 27:20, 1 Corinthiens 9:10; παρ᾽ ἐλπίδα, Romains 4:18; ἐπ᾽ ἐλπίδι, 1 Corinthiens 9:10. 
__2. Of religious hope: ἐπ᾽ ἐλπίδι, Actes 2:26 26:6, Romains 4:18 8:20, Tite 1:2; τῇ ἐ. ἐσώθημεν, Romains 8:24; κατ᾽ ἐλπίδα ζωῆς αἰωνίου, Tite 3:7; of the Messianic hope of Israel, Actes 23:6 26:6-7 28:20; of Christian hope, Romains 5:2-5 12:12 15:4, 13, 1 Corinthiens 13:13, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:16, Hébreux 3:6 6:11 7:19 10:23, 1 Pierre 1:3 1:21 3:15; with genitive obj., Romains 5:2, Colossiens 1:27, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:3 5:8, Tite 1:2; with genitive of that on which the hope is based, Actes 26:6, Éphésiens 1:18 4:4, Colossiens 1:23; ὁ θεὸς τῆς ἐ., Romains 15:13; ἔχειν ἐ. (= cl. ἐλπίζειν), Actes 24:15, Romains 15:4, 2 Corinthiens 3:12 10:15, Éphésiens 2:12, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:13; before ἐπί, with dative, 1 Jean 3:3; εἰς, Actes 24:15; ὅτι, Romains 8:20, Philippiens 1:20-21. Meton., 
__(a) of the author or ground of hope (cl.): 1 Thessaloniciens 2:19, 1 Timothée 1:1; with genitive obj., Colossiens 1:27; 
__(b) of the thing hoped for: Galates 5:5, Colossiens 1:5, Tite 2:13, Hébreux 6:18 (Cremer, 252, 712).†

G1681.def:
Ἐλύμας, -α, ὁ
(Aram. or Arab., cf. DB, i, 246 b) 
Elymas: Actes 13:8.†

G1682.def:
ἐλωί
(-ΐ Rec.; ἑλωΐ LT; Aram. אֱלָהּ), 
Eloi: Matthieu 27:46, Marc 15:34" (LXX) .†

G1684.def:
ἐμ-βαίνω 
[in LXX for עָלָה, etc. ;] 
to step into: Jean 5:4 (WH, RV omit); εἰς πλοῖον, to embark: Matthieu 8:23 9:1 13:2 14:22 15:39, Marc 4:1 5:18 6:45 8:10, 13, Luc 5:3 8:22, 37, Jean 6:17, 24 21:3, Actes 21:6.†

G1685.def:
ἐμ-βάλλω 
[in LXX for שׂוּם, etc. ;] 
to cast into: before εἰς, Luc 12:5 (cf. MM, Exp., vii, 93).†

G1686.def:
ἐμ-βάπτω 
to dip in: τ. χεῖρα ἐν τ. τρυβλίῳ, Matthieu 26:23; mid., before εἰς, Marc 14:20.†

G1687.def:
ἐμβατεύω 
[in LXX: with accusative, Josué 19:49 (נָחַל, Josué 19:51 (חָלַק pi.); before εἰς, 1Ma.12:25 1Mac 13:20 1Mac 14:31 1Mac 15:40; metaphorically, 2Ma.2:30 * ;] (ἐμβάτης ἐμβαίνω) 
__1. to step in or on (Soph.), hence 
__(a) to frequent, haunt, dwell in (Æsch., Eur.); metaphorically, Colossiens 2:18 (dwelling in, R, txt.; taking, R, mg.); 
__(b) to invade (1Mac, ll with; metaphorically, Col, Lc.). 
__2. to enter on, come into possession of (Eur., Dem.; LXX, Jos, H. with); on the difficulties of reading and interpretation in this passage, see Lft, Col., 194 f., 252; ICC, 268 ff.; Field, Notes, 197; Milligan, NTD, 177; and for exx. from π., MM, Exp., xii (cf. κενεμβ.).†

G1688.def:
ἐμ-βιβάζω 
[in LXX: 4Ki.9:23 (רָכַב hi.), Proverbes 4:11 (דָּרַךְ hi.) * ;] 
__1. to set in, put in. 
__2. to put on board ship, embark: with accusative of person(s), before εἰς, Actes 27:6.†

G1689.def:
ἐμ-βλέπω 
[in LXX for רָאָה, 3Ki.8:8, al.), פָּנָה (Job 6:28 A, al.); metaphorically, Ésaïe 51:1 (נָבַט hi.), Sir.2:10, etc. ;] 
to look at: with accusative of thing(s), Marc 8:25; with dative of person(s) (part., before λέγει, εἶπεν, cf. Xen., Cyr., i, 3, 2), Matthieu 19:26, Marc 10:21, 27 14:67, Luc 20:17 22:61 (ἐνέβλεψεν), Jean 1:36, 43; absol., to look, Actes 22:11; metaphorically, to consider: Matthieu 6:26.†

G1690.def:
ἐμ-βριμάομαι (T, -έομαι; Bl., § 22, 1), -ῶμαι 
(βρίμη, strength, bulk, whence βριμάομαι, to snort with anger), 
depon., with aor. mid. and pass., 
[in LXX (Hatch, Essays, 25): Dan LXX 11:30 (also Aq., Psaumes 7:12; Sm., Ésaïe 17:13) * ;] 
to snort in (of horses, Æsch.), hence, to speak or act with deep feeling (DCG, i, 62b); 
__(a) to be moved with anger (cf. ἐμβρίμημα, La 2:6): with dative, Marc 14:5, Jean 11:33; ἐν ἑαυτῷ, Jean 11:38; 
__(b) to admonish sternly: with dative, Matthieu 9:30, Marc 1:43.†

G1692.def:
ἐμέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 19:14 (קֵא)* ;] 
to vomit: figuratively, Apocalypse 3:16.†

G1693.def:
ἐμ-μαίνομαι depon., 
to rage against: with dative, Actes 26:11.†

G1694.def:
Ἐμμανουήλ, ὁ (Heb. עִמָּנוּאֵל, Ésaïe 7:14), 
Immanuel: Matthieu 1:23 (LXX).†

G1695.def:
Ἐμμαούς, ἡ
Emmaus, a place 60 furlongs from Jerusalem: Luc 24:13.†

G1696.def:
ἐμμένω 
[in LXX chiefly for קוּם ;] 
__1. to abide in: Actes 28:30. 
__2. to abide by, be true to: before ἐν; τ. πίστει, Actes 14:22; τ. διαθήκῃ, Hébreux 8:9 (LXX); with dative, τ. γεγραμμένοις (dative ptcp. as in legal formula; cf. Deiss., BS, 248; MM, Exp., xii): Galates 3:10 (LXX).†

G1697.def:
Ἑμμώρ (T, Ἐμμώρ, Rec. -όρ indecl. (Heb. חֲמוֹר), 
Emmor (Genèse 33:19): Actes 7:16.†
